items.fullText: 산업 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 AI 데이터센터용 SSD 수요 늘자…'케이스'도 호황 입력 2026.11.17 09:44 수정 2026.11.17 09:55 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 이광식 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. KX하이텍, 3분기 매출 524억원, 영업이익 97억원 '역대 최대' KX하이텍 주요 제품군(eSSD 케이스, IC Tray) 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터용 솔리드스테이트드라이브(SSD) 수요가 급증하면서 SSD를 감싸는 케이스를 생산하는 KX하이텍도 호황을 누리고 있다. 반도체 운반용 플라스틱 트레이와 SSD 케이스를 주력으로 생산하는 이 회사는 지난 3분기 역대 최대 실적을 기록했다. KX하이텍은 올해 3분기 연결 기준 매출 524억원, 영업이익 97억원을 기록했다고 17일 밝혔다. 지난해 같은 기간보다 각각 84.7%, 287.4% 증가한 수치다. 매출과 영업이익 모두 2분기 연속 분기 최대 실적을 경신했다. 올해 3분기까지 누적 매출은 1286억원으로 전년 동기 대비 45.5% 늘었다. 누적 영업이익은 245억원으로 497% 급증했다. 실적 개선을 이끈 것은 기업용 SSD(eSSD) 케이스다. SSD는 낸드플래시 메모리를 이용해 데이터를 저장하는 장치로, AI 데이터센터에서 대용량 데이터를 빠르게 저장하고 불러오는 데 사용된다. KX하이텍은 SSD 자체가 아니라 내부 부품을 감싸고 보호하는 외장 케이스를 생산한다. AI 서버와 데이터센터 투자가 늘면서 고용량 SSD 수요가 증가하자 케이스 주문도 함께 늘어난 것이다. 회사에 따르면 SSD 케이스 매출은 374억원으로 전년 동기 대비 75.4% 증가했다. 반도체 제조공정에서 사용하는 플라스틱 트레이도 주요 제품이다. 트레이는 반도체 칩이나 메모리 모듈을 담아 공정 간 이동·보관할 때 사용하는 부품이다. 반도체를 외부 충격 등으로부터 보호하는 역할을 한다. 회사 측은 반도체용 트레이 역시 견조한 성장세를 이어가고 있다고 설명했다. KX하이텍 2026년 3분기 실적 요약표 KX하이텍은 늘어나는 주문에 대응하기 위해 베트남 생산시설을 증설하고 있다. 지난 8월에는 110억원 규모의 전환사채(CB)를 발행했다. 증설 대상은 SSD 케이스와 반도체용 IC 트레이, 모듈 트레이 등이다. 회사 관계자는 “고용량·고기능 SSD 시장의 변화에 맞춰 생산라인을 신속하게 구축하고 안정화해 고객 수요에 대응하겠다”고 말했다. 이광식 기자 bumeran@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 이광식 기자 한국경제신문 중소기업부 소속 이광식 기자입니다. items.t: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
items.d: The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.
items.fullText: OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General’s office , alleging that the company’s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public. At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise , in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies’ security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident , OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.” The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients. The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems , DseWiki , the Wikimedia Foundation , and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing. The complaint also alleges that dozens of similar incidents have occurred without public disclosure. “OpenAI has recently sent notices to dozens of additional third parties whose websites or internal systems have been infiltrated by OpenAI agents,” the complaint reads. “In some cases, OpenAI agents were able to access sensitive personally identifiable information, such as employee records containing names, birth dates, addresses, and more. The vast majority of these incidents have not been disclosed or discussed publicly by either OpenAI or by the affected third parties.” The central allegation is that OpenAI’s ongoing testing practices constitute a public nuisance because the lack of safety controls present an ongoing risk to the public. A secondary claim alleges unfair competition stemming from the marketing of an unsafe product. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors

items.t: California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents
items.d: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s lawsuit alleges OpenAI has created AI models without proper safeguards. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 OpenAI logo. Samuel Boivin / NurPhoto via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:52 PM EST / Updated Nov. 16, 2026, 2:34 PM EST By Daniel Arkin California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people. The suit centers on a July incident involving hundreds of autonomous AI agents created by OpenAI that attacked computer systems at Hugging Face , a separate AI company. Bonta’s office alleges the attack was “entirely foreseeable in light of OpenAI’s choice to test models it knew to be dangerous in a flawed and exploitable testing environment without proper oversight.” Bonta’s office further alleges the ChatGPT developer’s failure to secure the testing of its models created a “public nuisance” and violated California’s Unfair Competition Law, a broad consumer protection statute. In response to a request for comment, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has “undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity” since the Hugging Face incident. items.t: U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips in foreign data centers
items.d: The Commerce Department further restricted the sale of American AI chips, addressing concerns about how Chinese companies might evade U.S. export restrictions.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips through foreign data centers The Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday morning that it would clamp down on the sale of chips to data center customers in Southeast Asian countries. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced questions in recent months about why the department's Entity List had not been updated for over a year. Alex Brandon / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:44 PM EST By Jared Perlo The Commerce Department moved to further restrict the sale of top-tier American AI chips Monday morning, addressing mounting concerns about how companies in China and other countries might evade American export restrictions by taking advantage of longstanding loopholes. As part of a new rule, data center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil must now receive a special license from the Commerce Department in order to buy advanced AI chips from American companies such as Nvidia or AMD. Over the past several years, businesses in those countries have bought billions of dollars worth’ of high-end chips, raising concerns that some chips might be illegally smuggled into China. The rule, issued by the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, will also require existing overseas data center customers to receive a similar license if they provide “significant volumes” of computing power to companies whose headquarters are in China, Russia, Cuba or other countries banned from receiving certain types of advanced American technology. Companies in these countries have allowed Chinese businesses to access their most advanced AI chips remotely , skirting rules that prevented Chinese companies from accessing these chips on Chinese territory. items.fullText: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance November 16, 2026 by Shruti Koparkar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation. items.t: SKT가 짓는 AI 데이터센터…효성중공업 전력기술 심는다
items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 SKT가 짓는 AI 데이터센터…효성중공업 전력기술 심는다 입력 2026.11.16 17:48 수정 2026.11.17 01:40 지면 A13 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 라현진 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 초고압 변전설비 안정적 공급 국내외 신규사업도 공동 발굴 SK텔레콤과 효성중공업이 기가와트(GW)급 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터를 구축하기 위해 손을 잡았다. 양사는 16일 서울 을지로 SKT타워에서 ‘AI 데이터센터 구축을 위한 전략적 파트너십’ 업무협약(MOU)을 체결했다고 발표했다. 이번 협약에 따라 효성중공업은 SK텔레콤의 AI 데이터센터용 345킬로볼트(kV) 변전소에 핵심 전력 설비를 공급하기로 했다. 345kV 변전소는 초고압 송전망에서 대용량 전력을 공급받아 데이터센터에서 사용할 수 있는 전압으로 변환하는 시설이다. 양사가 MOU를 맺은 것은 AI 데이터센터가 대형화하면서 전력 설비를 제때 확보하는 일이 중요해지고 있기 때문이다. 특히 초고압 변압기는 주문부터 납품까지 최장 5년이나 걸린다. 확보가 늦어지면 데이터센터 건설과 가동 일정에도 차질이 생길 수 있다. 양사는 핵심 전력 설비의 생산과 납품 일정을 사전에 조율해 공급 안정성을 높이기로 했다. SK텔레콤의 데이터센터 개발·운영 경험과 효성중공업의 전력 설비 제조·엔지니어링 역량을 결합한다는 구상이다. 차세대 전력기술 개발에도 협력한다. 양사는 800볼트(V) 직류배전과 반도체 변압기(SST)의 공동 검토 및 실증을 추진한다. 800V 직류배전은 서버와 통신장비 가까이까지 전력을 직류로 공급해 전력 변환 단계를 줄이는 기술이다. 이를 통해 전력 손실과 설비 부담을 줄일 수 있을 것으로 기대한다. 초고압 변전설비의 운영·유지보수 기술과 현장 경험도 공유한다. 데이터센터의 안정적인 가동을 지원하는 동시에 협력 범위를 신규 데이터센터의 사업개발과 구축 분야로 확대할 방침이다. 국내외 사업 기회를 공동 발굴하고 협력형 사업모델도 검토할 계획이다. 정재헌 SK텔레콤 최고경영자(CEO)는 “핵심 전력 인프라를 안정적으로 확보하고 협력을 확장하는 계기가 될 것”이라고 말했다. 우태희 효성중공업 대표는 “SK텔레콤은 물론 SK그룹과도 장기적인 전략적 파트너십을 확대해 AI 데이터센터 전력 시장에서 시너지를 내겠다”고 밝혔다. 라현진 기자 raraland@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 라현진 기자 안녕하세요. 한국경제신문 테크&사이언스부 라현진 기자입니다. 인공지능(AI), 소프트웨어, 통신, 클라우드, OTT 등 IT 산업 전반과 과학기술정보통신부, 개인정보보호위원회와 방송미디어통신위원회를 출입하고 있습니다. 앞서 유통산업부에서 오프라인 유통, 소비재, e커머스, 패션·뷰티 분야를 취재했습니다. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Contribution and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Representatives from the Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA met with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. items.fullText: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion.
